title: Access tiers: hot, cool, cold and archive, with the rehydration wait

videos.script: Every blob from the last two lessons sat in the same place: the hot tier. That is the default, and the most expensive shelf to keep things on. {{shelf}} Azure has three cheaper ones. Cool, cold and archive. Each keeps a gigabyte for less, and charges more to take it back. {{tiers}} Three of them answer in milliseconds. The fourth does not answer at all. {{archive}} You will archive one of Quitanda's exports and try to read it. Azurite refuses, the way Azure does. {{refuse}} Then you bring it back. Azurite does it at once. Azure takes up to fifteen hours. {{rehydrate}} And every cooler tier has a minimum stay. Leave early and you pay for the days you did not stay. {{minimum}} A short program puts a terabyte in each tier for a year, with prices you replace by the real ones. {{year}} By the end you can look at a set of files, ask how often they are read and how long they stay, and name their tier. {{end}}
